document.activity: Wall & Floor Tiling – Preparation and Laying
document.jobDescription: General wall and floor tiling works + waterproofing

monitoring: Regular inspections and observations will be conducted by Giuseppe Ciccone to ensure SWMS is being complied with.
Daily Toolbox Talks will be undertaken to identify, control and communicate additional site hazards.
Work must cease immediately if incident or near miss occurs. SWMS must be amended in consultation with relevant people.
Amendments must be approved by Giuseppe Ciccone and communicated to all affected workers before work resumes.
SWMS must be made available for inspection or review as required by WHS legislation.
Record of SWMS must be kept as required by WHS legislation (until job is complete or for 2 years if involved in a notifiable incident).

ppe.general: Safety footwear, eye protection, gloves & knee protectors. Ensure all PPE meets relevant Australian Standards. Inspect, and replace PPE as needed.
ppe.whereRequired: Hearing protection, high visibility shirt or vest & breathing protection.

safetyNotes.text: Cement is classified as a hazardous chemical according to the Australian Safety and Compensation Council (ASCC) formerly (NOHSC) and is not classified as a dangerous good according to Australian Code for the Transport of Dangerous Goods by Road or Rail. Efforts should be made to avoid inhalation of cement dust and avoid direct skin contact. Minimise generation of cement dust – Mix outside and/or wear a P1 respirator. Cement has a very powerful caustic effect on skin due to its alkaline content and has the potential to cause burns and dermatitis. Rubber or PVC gloves should be worn when working with cement and cement-based products (concrete, mortar, mud)

Sand is classified as a hazardous chemical according to the ASCC and is not classified as a dangerous good according to Australian Code for the Transport of Dangerous Goods by Road or Rail. Sand (crystalline silica) has the potential to cause damage to the lungs (scarring). Efforts should be made to keep sand wet to avoid dust generation and inhalation of particles. Safety goggles & dust mask should be worn when generating dust through machining (grinding).

The majority of cement-based adhesives (all powders) are classified as hazardous chemical according to the ASCC and are not classified as dangerous goods according to Australian Code for the Transport of Dangerous Goods by Road or Rail. Generation of dust should be avoided. Mixing powders should be performed outside and respiratory protection is advised. Eye protection should be worn when mixing / stirring. Gloves (rubber / PVA / neoprene) should be worn when mixing. Seek further clarification from specific product SDS where required.

The majority of grouting compounds (all powders) are classified as a hazardous chemical according to the ASCC and are not classified as dangerous goods according to Australian Code for the Transport of Dangerous Goods by Road or Rail. Continued handling of grouting compounds is known to cause dermatitis. To reduce risk PVC gloves should be worn when handling. Safety glasses are advised when mixing grouts. Seek further clarification from specific product SDS where required.

tasks.task: Personnel Requirements – Before commencing any work on site
hazards: Injury may occur to personnel not trained in the correct use of equipment and are unaware of Site-Specific Conditions that may affect working procedures.

controls.heading: Training: Should include:
items: Safe work procedures
Fitting of personal protective equipment
Manual handling, plant safety (grinders)

controls.heading: Induction: Where required, all people carrying out tiling activities should participate in relevant training including:
items: Construction Induction
Site Specific Induction
Safe Work Procedures;
Hazard identification processes;
Control measures including PPE;
Manual handling, machinery & height safety.

tasks.task: Preparation – Identify work area, preparation & setup

controls.heading: Ensure:
items: The floor or working area is free from rubbish and debris, and clear access is available for all workers.
Erect any barriers & signage
Keep power leads up off the ground and out of the way and all power tools and leads are Tested and Tagged and are current.
Use correct manual handling techniques when handling adhesives, tiles, cement
Work area is set up to avoid manual handling risks, trips and falls and that an adequate area is available (external) for mixing & cutting activities

tasks.task: Operation – Mixing & spreading Sand / Cement & Adhesives

controls.heading: Manual handling:
items: Where possible have builder position tiles into accessible location using crane / forklift
Use trolleys to transfer boxes of tiles, cements, adhesives, grout to the work area
Instruct relevant workers to only handle loads within limitations or ask for assistance.

controls.heading: Mixing and applying:
items: When mixing powders, ensure that relevant PPE is worn (respiratory protection, gloves, eye protection)
When using cement mixer for mortar, ensure mixer is positioned on level stable ground, leads positioned clear of water and cement / sand positioned in close proximity
Conduct mixing tasks outside to enable air movement to disperse dusts – Add powder to water to reduce dust generation
When using electric drill to mix powders tuck in loose clothing and tie back hair.
Ensure that the tool and leads are tested and tagged with correct date and that all leads are protected from water immersion and other damage.
Keep all non-essential personnel clear of mixing activities
Use appropriate Tool (Trowel / shovel) to evenly spread product - avoiding unnecessary splattering
Wash up all tools / skin with water whilst still wet to aid in removal of product

controls.heading: Cutting & Laying Tiles:
items: Prior to laying tiles ensure that knee pads are fitted
When cutting tiles with 4” grinder (fitted with diamond blade) only does so outside clear of other personnel – Place barriers / signage to keep nonessential personnel clear of the work area
Check condition of tool, integrity of blade & placement of lead
Wear safety glasses, hearing protection and respiratory protection when using grinder
Place all offcuts in a safe position to avoid cluttering and creating untidy work areas
When using Tile Cutter ensure that the tool is placed on a stable / level surface take caution when handling cut tiles as sharp edges may be present – wear gloves when handling
Position tiles to reduce manual handling risks / reduce distances travelled and double handling

controls.heading: Tiling at Height:
items: Where tiles (wall) are required to be positioned at height, ensure that suitable platform ladders or trestle (No >2.0m) are used.
Ensure ladders are suitable to task, industrial rated and adequately restrained from falling
When tiling at height – a second person should be present to provide assistance and expedite task.

controls.heading: Silica dust management
items: Dust Suppression – cut tiles with a wet tile saw
Dust Extraction – cut tiles with an angle grinder with a shroud attached to a HEPA vacuum cleaner
At all times you are not exposing your workers or other workers to airborne silica dust

controls.heading: Manual handling:
items: Use trolleys to transfer boxes / containers of grout to the work area
Instruct relevant workers to only handle loads within limitations or ask for assistance

controls.heading: Mixing and applying:
items: When mixing powders, ensure that relevant PPE is worn (respiratory protection, gloves, eye protection)
Conduct mixing tasks outside to enable air movement to disperse dusts – Add grout to water to reduce generation of dust
When using electric drill to mix grout (if in powder form) tuck in loose clothing and tie back hair.
Ensure that the tool and leads are tested and tagged with correct date and that all leads are protected from water immersion and other damage.
Keep all nonessential personnel clear of mixing activities
Use appropriate tool / applicator to evenly spread product - avoiding unnecessary splattering
Wear gloves and eye protection to avoid contact with wet products
Wash up all tools / skin with water whilst still wet to aid in removal of product
Remove excess grout with wet sponge – Wear gloves

controls.heading: Personal Hygiene:
items: Wash all exposed skin with water. The use of soap will also assist with the removal of cement-based products

controls.heading: Tools:
items: Wash all tools with water

controls.heading: Excess cement / sand / mortar / adhesive /grout:
items: Must not be allowed to enter any drain or storm water system.
Place in small stacks (about a full shovel) and allow drying for safe removal.
Place in bin provided by Builder

controls.heading: Other:
items: Remove any barricades if no longer required.
Place all rubbish in the appropriate bins.
Site to be left in clean and tidy condition ready for handover to Builder / Contract Manager who is to be advised upon completion of works

controls.heading: Set up access (ladder/scaffold)
items: Use secured ladder or scaffold, check before use

controls.heading: Work at height
items: Install edge protection or covers, no overreaching

controls.heading: Use of ladder
items: 3 points of contact, short duration only, secure ladder

controls.heading: Tools/materials at height
items: Keep area tidy, set exclusion zone

controls.heading: Weather (external)
items: Stop working in unsafe weather

controls.heading: Harness (if needed)
items: Use harness & approved anchor point

controls.heading: Emergency
items: Rescue plan, first aid available

likelihood.description: Expected in most circumstances. Effect is a common result
Will probably occurs in most circumstances. Effect is known to have occurred at this site, or it has happened
Might occur at some time. Effect could occur at the site, or I've heard of it happening
Could occur at some time. Effect is not likely to occur at the site, or I have not heard of it happening
May occur only in exceptional circumstances. Effect is practically impossible.

consequence.example: No effect – or so minor that effect is acceptable
First aid treatment only; spillage contained at site.
Medical treatment; spillage contained but with outside help.

riskAssessment.matrixNote: Risk Management Code of Practice 2007, AS/NZS 31000-2009 Risk Management Principles and guidelines. Step 1 Determine Likelihood – What is the possibility that the effect will occur? Step 2 Determine Consequence - What will be the expected effect? Step 3 Determine the risk score. Step 4 Record risk score on worksheet (Note – Risk scores have no absolute value and should only be used for comparison and to engender discussion.)

riskLegend.label: A: Acute – ACT NOW – Urgent - do something about the risks immediately. Requires immediate attention.
H: High – Highest management decision is required urgently.
L: Low – OK for now. Record and review regularly, and if any equipment/ people/ materials/ work processes or procedures change.
